thread:
carla: quick follow-up from today's shard fairness deep-dive. want to capture one alternative we didn't land on: CRDT-like credit convergence vs lease-first migrations.

dennis: CRDTs are elegant for eventual convergence but messy for hard quotas. if we allow additive counters to converge, legal/billing caps become fuzzy.

hana: agree. maybe hybrid: use commutative counters for best-effort credits (burst spill) and a strong lease/slow-path for hard caps. label dimensions as BEST_EFFORT vs MUST_FAIL.

theo: hybrid sounds practical. operational concern: how do we prevent duplicate consumption when a tenant is migrated and cached credits exist on old shard?

carla: short TTL on cached credits + migration fence. on migration we write a migration marker and invalidate caches; recipients reject tokens with pre-migration nonces.

dennis: proposal for API: issue spill token: `{tenant, capacity, expiry, nonce, sig}`; donor publishes migration marker `migration:{tenant, gen}`. recipients check marker.gen >= token.gen to allow.

hana: adds writes on migration but common case stays local. also need global abuse flags: central append-only ledger + push channel for urgent blocks. shards cache with 1s ttl.

theo: simulation tasks: 1) 50k tenants, skew 1-1000x, 2) churn where 5% shards crash mid-migration, 3) enforcement test for MUST_FAIL quotas. measure false-overage rate and migration oscillation.

carla: rollout: feature-flagged CRDT counters for BEST_EFFORT on 5% traffic, enable spill-tokens after telemetry looks stable, then lease/migration for medium tenants.

ops-bot: created ticket INFRA-1899 "credit-convergence vs lease hybrid follow-up" and linked this thread.

hana: i'll take the ledger + urgent-push design.

dennis: i'll prototype token signature + migration marker semantics.

carla: thanks — we'll sync next infra-arch. :sparkles:
